plain_english: In the range of lust, anger, greed, delusion, pride and envy — intellect uncaused having been made, that reality remains.
sanskrit_cite: kāmakrodhalobhamohamadamātsaryagocare | buddhiṃ nistimitāṃ kṛtvā tat tattvam avaśiṣyate

plain_english: The world, Indra-net-made, cast — or picture-work-like; whirling, or the meditating one's all: and seeing — joy upsurges.
sanskrit_cite: indrajālamayaṃ viśvaṃ vyastaṃ vā citrakarmavat | bhramad vā dhyāyataḥ sarvam paśyataś ca sukhodgamaḥ

plain_english: Not into pain should the mind be cast, not into joy, nor scattered about: O Bhairavī — in the middle, what reality remains may be known.
sanskrit_cite: na cittaṃ nikṣiped duḥkhe na sukhe vā parikṣipet | bhairavi jñāyatāṃ madhye kiṃ tattvam avaśiṣyate

plain_english: Having left the own-body-standing, contemplating everywhere-I-am-thus: with firm mind, by a gaze not seeing elsewhere — happy may he be.
sanskrit_cite: vihāya nijadehasthaṃ sarvatrāsmīti bhāvayan | dṛḍhena manasā dṛṣṭyā nānyekṣiṇyā sukhī bhavet

plain_english: In a pot and such — whatever knowing; desire and such, or inside me: never all-pervading born — contemplating thus, all-going.
sanskrit_cite: ghaṭādau yac ca vijñānam icchādyaṃ vā mamāntare | naiva sarvagataṃ jātam bhāvayan iti sarvagaḥ

plain_english: Grasper-grasped awareness: common to all embodied; of yogins the distinction but — He is, in relation, carefulness.
sanskrit_cite: grāhyagrāhakasaṃvittiḥ sāmānyā sarvadehinām | yogināṃ tu viśeṣo =B9sti sambandhe sāvadhānatā

plain_english: Like self in another body — He even should perceive awareness: regard of one's own body having left, pervasive in days may he be.
sanskrit_cite: svavad anyaśarīre =B9pi saṃvittim anubhāvayet | apekṣāṃ svaśarīrasya tyaktvā vyāpī dinair bhavet

plain_english: Supportless mind having been made — thoughts should not be thought: then, in self-supreme-self — Bhairava, O deer-eyed one.
sanskrit_cite: nirādhāraṃ manaḥ kṛtvā vikalpān na vikalpayet | tadātmaparamātmatve bhairavo mṛgalocane

plain_english: All-knowing, all-doing, and pervasive, the highest Lord: he indeed I — Śiva-natured; hence from firmness, Śiva may one be.
sanskrit_cite: sarvajñaḥ sarvakartā ca vyāpakaḥ parameśvaraḥ | sa evāhaṃ śaivadharmā iti dārḍhyāc chivo bhavet

plain_english: Like the waves of water, the flame-plays of fire, the sun's light: of me indeed, of Bhairava — these world-plays, manifested.
sanskrit_cite: jalasyevormayo vahner jvālābhaṅgyaḥ prabhā raveḥ | mamaiva bhairavasyaitā viśvabhaṅgyo vibheditāḥ
